_README: Hand-curated gold labels, keyed on the 8-char correlation prefix used throughout
WHY HAND-CURATED, NOT PARSED: there is exactly ONE RUBRIC_*.md in the repo, and
~21 lines in a 141KB notes file carry a grade, in at least four incompatible prose
shapes (a prospective grading key; two markdown tables with DIFFERENT columns;
inline bolded prose; a narrative run-ledger carrying several runs at once). The
value vocabulary is open ('partial', '**PASS, CITED**', '**FAIL - and actively
dismissed**', 'not reached', 'abstained (neutral)'). Worst of all, several uses of
FAILED mean an API 529 or a lost spawn, NOT a rubric grade - a regex would
confidently mislabel those as negatives, which is the one error a benchmark cannot
absorb. Enumerating ~10 runs by hand is faster and correct.
STATUS: INCOMPLETE - only entries this thread could ground in evidence it actually
read are present. Do not treat absence as 'ungraded'; treat it as 'not yet
curated'. Completing it means reading NOTES_running_fixloop(10).md end to end.
FIELDS: benchmark_grade PASS|PARTIAL|FAIL|null (null = no rubric grade, including
when a run died of infrastructure); terminal merged|approved|escalated|rejected|
BLINDING: this file is never concatenated into input_state. It ships separately
and joins at emit time, so the corpus cannot leak the benchmark's own answers.
